fatal.reason: OPEN DEFECT (Plan A outcome, Family A) awaiting Phase B fix, NOT an adjudicated/acceptable FATAL. `double` is passed by name to `.into_iter().map(double)` -- a function used as a VALUE, never as a direct call. walk.rs:94 only resolves ast::CallExpr with a PathExpr callee, so passing a function's name as a value produces no CallExpr at all and therefore no edge. rustc compiles `vec![1,2,3].into_iter().map(double).collect()` and emits no dead_code warning for `double`; the helper has no incoming edge to it and no root reaches it, so it reads dead. This is the exact false-dead-code failure the Plan A outcome section documents for this family -- fix tracked for Phase B (walk.rs must resolve function-valued PathExpr/array-literal/let-binding contexts, not just CallExpr callees), not suppressed or excluded here.
